newsitem.title: USA: NationsBank offers credit line to N.C. arena group.
newsitem.headline: NationsBank offers credit line to N.C. arena group.

text.p: NationsBank Corp has offered a $5 million line of credit to the Raleigh, N.C., sports authority seeking to build a $120 million arena, the financial adviser to the Centennial Authority said on Tuesday.
"It's a small but important step," said Edward Boyles of the Robinson-Humphrey Co Inc, the financial adviser.
However, he said, "It's very, very preliminary."

The newly created authority has $72 million for the project, including $22 million pledged by boosters for North Carolina State University. The arena would house the university's basketball team and possibly a professional sports team.
"They need about another $48 million to complete the project," Boyles said.

The Centennial Authority hopes to issue $48 million in revenue bonds or possibly certificates of participation to help finance the 21,300-seat arena. But it must first work out an agreement with the City of Raleigh and Wake County on how to divide the Wake County hotel tax revenue that would pay debt service.
"They are also still working out some things with North Carolina State University," Boyles said.
If an agreement can be reached, the debt probably would be a negotiated issue, and would be the first by the authority, he said.
"As for the timing of when they'll draw that money down or use that financing, it would be (too soon to comment on exact timing) " Boyles said.
